draft.title: How do I stop doomscrolling at two in the morning?
draft.description: Doomscrolling can feel like an endless cycle, especially in the quiet hours of the night. If you find yourself scrolling through news feeds or social media at two in the morning, it’s important to recognize that you're not alone, and there are practical steps you can take to break this habit.
draft.shortAnswer: To stop doomscrolling at two in the morning, set boundaries for your screen time, create a calming bedtime routine, and replace scrolling with more restful activities like reading or journaling.

sections.heading: Before you start
sections.body: Understanding your triggers is the first step. Ask yourself what prompts you to reach for your phone at night. Is it boredom, anxiety, or the need for connection? Recognizing these triggers can help you develop healthier habits.
bullets: Identify specific emotions that lead to doomscrolling.
Reflect on what you hope to gain from scrolling.
Consider the impact of late-night scrolling on your sleep.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.body: Here’s a simple plan to help you reduce doomscrolling:
bullets: Set a specific time to put your phone away each night.
Create a calming bedtime routine that doesn’t involve screens.
Use apps that limit your social media access during certain hours.
Keep your phone out of reach from your bed.

sections.heading: What to say
sections.body: When you feel the urge to scroll, try saying to yourself, "I choose to prioritize my rest and mental health right now." This affirmation can help reinforce your decision to step away from your device.
bullets: Practice self-compassion; it’s okay to feel overwhelmed.
Remind yourself of the benefits of a good night's sleep.
Visualize a peaceful morning free from the stress of late-night scrolling.

sections.heading: What gets in the way
sections.body: Several barriers may prevent you from stopping doomscrolling, such as:
bullets: The addictive nature of social media and news.
Fear of missing out (FOMO) on important updates.
Anxiety that prompts you to seek reassurance through news.

sections.heading: How to tell it is working
sections.body: You’ll know your efforts are paying off when you notice:
bullets: Improved sleep quality and feeling more rested in the morning.
Less anxiety or stress related to news consumption.
A greater sense of control over your evening routine.

sections.heading: Next step
sections.body: If you find that you’re still struggling despite these strategies, consider reaching out for support. Whether through coaching or therapy, professional guidance can help you explore deeper issues that contribute to your nighttime habits.
bullets: Look into virtual therapy options if you are in Tennessee.
Join a support group focused on digital wellness.
